overview.title: Salt air after the medina
overview.p1: Martil is Tetouan’s beach outlet: a small Mediterranean town with a corniche, seasonal crowds and simple seafood restaurants. It is close enough for an afternoon without changing hotels.
overview.p2: Come for a swim, a walk along the front, and grilled fish. It is not a remote wild beach — expect a developed seafront — but it resets the senses after dense white lanes.
overview.p3: Summer weekends are busiest. Shoulder seasons feel calmer and still swimmable on warm days.

q1.question: How far from Tetouan?
q1.answer: Short taxi or local bus ride — typically under 30 minutes depending on traffic.

q2.question: Worth an overnight?
q2.answer: Only if you want consecutive beach days. Most travellers day-trip from Tetouan.

q3.question: Family friendly?
q3.answer: Yes — easy beach access and restaurants. Supervise swimming as on any open coast.

q4.question: Best season?
q4.answer: Late spring through early autumn for swimming; winter for walks and fresh air.

food.title: Seafood on the coast
food.p1: Martil’s draw for many visitors is grilled fish and simple seafood plates facing the sea.
food.p2: Agree roughly on fish prices when ordering by weight. Busy local tables are a good sign.
